correctness.rationale: The standard depth-one residual least-squares formula is used directly. The map is a strict diagonal positive contraction with an explicit positive fixed point and positive monotone Picard iterates. Scaling the slow coordinate gives an exact nondegenerate limiting Anderson recurrence whose sixth second coordinate is strictly negative while preceding coordinates are positive; rational dependence yields the open-family result. The packaged checker exactly verifies the rational witness and the one-dimensional fixed-point identity.

value.rationale: Positive fixed-point maps occur when coordinates represent concentrations, probabilities, populations, or nonnegative factors. The result isolates a minimal failure mechanism showing that residual-minimizing extrapolation can violate the cone even without coupling or nonlinearity. The exact witness is useful for safeguards and regression tests, and the one-dimensional impossibility distinguishes a genuine multivariate effect.
